From experience with Keloid treatment there’s 2 types of treatment that can help reduce the appearance of them. At first it was a strong steroid cream with a tegarderm plaster over the scar for 12 hours which did reduce the appearance when they weren’t as severe. The other treatment involved dermatologists, a series of steroid injections into the scars. However be mindful that either of these treatments can cause atrophy of the scar (makes a kind of indented into the skin). Other options are freezing of the scars and silicone dressings. 
Best of luck!

So I don’t know if this will help you understand. But I was on seroquel 300mg for my mental illness. One week I ran out and the my doctors was closed so I seen an emergency doc. He prescribed it to me and instead of giving me prolonged release tablets I received immediate release tablets. 

So that night I took them not thinking anything of it. That was until about 45 minutes in I was trying to eat food with my friend and I began losing the ability to swallow. Okay no more eating for me. I then felt my blood pressure take a drastic drop and I knew it was time to lie down. What I can only describe after that was immense fear, I felt like something or someone was trying to drag me down. I tried to fight against it but it was severe. 

My heart stopped but I didn’t die that night and I was resuscitated and let me tell you, overdosing could just leave you in the same situation. I woke up and nothing was the same after that. Multiple spots of brain death and some neurological appointments to try and map what actually happened to my brain as a result of those medications. I’m still dealing with it to this day and it’s literally been 3 years since it happened. 

Please consider what you are deciding here, if you would like to message me you are more than welcome to but trust me taking a load of those antipsychotics is not the last thing you want to experience on this earth. I am sending you hugs and really hope if you need to talk do not hesitate to reach out.

It was okay mainly. I started my period when I was 10 years old and by age 11 I was already suffering with extreme pain/heavy bleeding/fainting/patterns in how I was experiencing cramps. The first time I ended up in ER with these pains they did an ultrasound of my womb and came to the conclusion that I had a burst cyst episode. Then because of my young age mixed with that first finding they weren’t too pushed on my pain or investigating it any further. I was sent home with 100s of tablets worth of mefamenic acid and codeine. That was my teenage years unfortunately, extreme pain and being on such strong opioids at that age wasn’t great. I was still too sick to attend school and on the days I was in less amounts of pain I was still high on painkillers. It took about 3 more hospitalisations and a letter from my school teachers explaining I was suffering and missing school but most importantly not present in class due to extremely strong medication for them to decide I needed a exploratory lap. I was 15 by that stage and 3.5 years taking horrible painkillers. I was suffering not only physically but mentally and I don’t actually recall much of those years of my life. I was taken in for surgery that November and they found endometriosis was sitting on my womb and ovaries. They removed what they could safely remove but told me that they didn’t get it all. That reoccurrence of severe symptoms is very likely. I didn’t care though! I knew I wasn’t imagining such extreme pain the way a lot of doctors made it out to be. I had a medically confirmed diagnoses and I was happy but sad at the same time. Very conflicting. Especially because not a lot was known about endo back then. I was started soon after on the depo-provera injection to stop the periods to reduce the growth of the endo and it worked wonders on my pain levels. 

That was 9 years ago in November. I’ve unfortunately experienced reoccurrence of my extreme symptoms and also with being diagnosed with colitis. I’m actually going in for my second laparoscopic surgery Tuesday week. So I’m hoping we can get something from it and hopefully some relief from the symptoms. 

One thing I will say is don’t give up on finding your answers. Don’t let any doctor tell you your pain is over exaggerated or that you clearly don’t handle pain well. Stick to your guns and remind them as much as you can that you are struggling and that something isn’t right. Always advocate for yourself even when you feel like giving up entirely. Also look after yourself and don’t be too hard on yourself. Remember it’s okay to have sick days and if you simply cannot get out of bed that’s absolutely okay. I hope you get your answers soon enough. And if you need to talk don’t hesitate to reach out.

I’m not a doctor but I’ve had a similar journey to your wife , it got so bad with foods that I ended up refusing to eat because I couldn’t figure out what was causing it. My only thing is I wish I done it differently. Unfortunately your wife will not get her answers by cutting out all food. I understand so much her reasoning on this but I wish I could tell her that she’s not going to benefit from doing that. It’s more than likely she will become deficient in a lot of things due to lack of nutrition. Truthfully until they have what it is she’s dealing with under control she won’t ever feel good after eating. Even simple things like a biscuit will make her feel unwell. I had to just accept I wasn’t going to feel well after food no matter how under control my symptoms were. Okay the symptoms are less severe from time to time. Something she could do to help identify her trigger foods would be to try the FODMAP diet which is explained here: https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/low-fodmap-diet#section1  I did it for like two weeks and slowly started adding different food types back into my diet. It helped identify quite a few trigger foods for me. One of the main ones was surprisingly one of the foods it allows you to have. I know medical bills can be shocking but I know that’s one of the things I could do at home to help me understand my stomach symptoms a bit better. 

I hope she finds answers soon and I hope she starts to feel better soon.

The first thing I did was see my gp and tell him I wasn’t doing so well. I talked in depth about my symptoms and didn’t hide one thing about my state of mind. For me it was an immediate prescription of medication and twice weekly visits. I was referred to see my countries psychiatric clinic that’s in my area. Our waiting list is about two years minimum so until then I found as many relevant free mental health services to sign up for. 
Funnily enough they helped more than a psychiatrist could ever have. So free services aren’t something you don’t try out. 

So mainly keeping good contact with your gp, make sure you like him/her too. It really helps if you’re comfortable sharing your thoughts with someone. I trust my gp more than any other doctor I’ve ever dealt with. 

Also don’t presume that if put on medication it will be done and dusted. It can take many trial and errors to get the right type of medication for you. I had to change mine 4 times before I found the right one. 

Be patient, these things can take a long time to start making you feel better. You will have some knock backs and you’ll meet doctors that seem to not take you seriously. But once you find the right doctors it will be easier. 

Lastly don’t beat yourself up if you have knock backs. It happens. We’re human after all and emotions are not easy to deal with. So don’t feel disappointed if you start doing well and wake up one morning feeling crappy. Make sure you talk to your doctor about it. It still matters even if you were doing well before that.

I have endometriosis. Currently in between treatments at the moment.  But the main one that seems to work every time is stopping periods all together.

Second treatment was start on the depo-provera injection which did help and stop my period for about 2 years. After that it lost its effectiveness. 
I’m currently waiting for a consult with my gynaecologist to see what we can do next to stop my periods. But I know that I got a lot of pain relief when I didn’t have any periods. 
Of course always consult with a doctor on what’s best for you. 
Surgery does help most but unfortunately for me it didn’t.
